result.title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
result.summary: Large reasoning models (LRMs) that leverage test-time computation achieve strong performance on mathematical and scientific benchmarks and are increasingly deployed in real-world applications. However, their ability to perform \textit{everyday logical reasoning}, which often departs from textbook formal logic, remains underexplored. In this work, we systematically evaluate how well reasoning models align with everyday reasoning patterns by introducing a benchmark based on linguistic and pragmatic reasoning phenomena. We also compare reasoning models with non-reasoning models under controlled prompting conditions. We find that, in many cases, (1) reasoning models show degraded performance in everyday reasoning when such reasoning deviates from formal logical rules, (2) some non-reasoning models with chain-of-thought prompting outperform comparable reasoning models in everyday reasoning, and (3) prompting with additional instructions provides limited control over reasoning behavior. These findings suggest that current reasoning models do not reliably capture everyday reasoning and point to limitations in post-training, motivating improved training objectives and evaluation across diverse forms of reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建基于语言与语用推理现象的基准，系统评测大型推理模型在日常逻辑推理上是否与人类日常推理模式一致，并在受控提示条件下与非推理模型（含 CoT）对比，发现当日常推理偏离形式逻辑时推理模型表现下降、部分 CoT 非推理模型反而更优、额外指令提示对推理行为的控制有限。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本推理模型评测、不涉及视觉输入或 latent 状态，但其「提示难以控制推理行为」与「显式长推理未必优于非推理模型」的结论，可供核查 LVR 中显式/隐式推理形式、推理长度与停止控制、计算预算收益成本的评价设计线索。
